3 has preferred MFA No.6847/2021 and respondent No.2 therein has preferred MFA No.6765/2019.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
That on 28.09.2016 the deceased - Krishnaiah along with his wife and son, who are petitioners, while traveling on the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA.06Q.4203 stopped the same near Kondli cross on Honnenahalli road to talk to one of his relative who was also passing by the same road.

At that time, 407 tempo bearing registration No.KA.02.C.5054 duly insured with the second respondent - Insurance Company being driven in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed against the motor cycle.
Because of which, the said Krishnaiah sustained grievous injuries and died.

4. The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.20,10,272/- along with interest @ 6% p.a. under the following heads:-
Love and affection Rs.20,000/-
Transportation and Funeral Rs.20,000/-
expenses Loss of consortium Rs.40,000/-
Loss of Estate Rs.15,000/-
Loss of Dependency Rs.19,15,272/-
 Total Rs.20,10,272/-
5.
Aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company has preferred MFA No.6765/2019 and the petitioners have preferred MFA No.6847/2021 for enhancement of compensation.
6. The case of the respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is that the accident has not taken place as alleged.
But it is seen that the Insurance Company has not examined any witness in its support.
On the contrary, petitioner No.1 has examined herself and has spoken as to how the accident has taken place.
Her evidence has not been impeached in the cross examination.
Her evidence is further supported by IMV and medical report as well as the sketch prepared by the police.
All these aspects corroborates that the accident did take place as alleged by the petitioners.
7. It is further submitted that subsequent to the accident, criminal proceedings have been initiated against the driver of the tempo.

The Branch Manager vs Smt. Drakshayini on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89003179/
4
8. All the above aspects prove that accident took place as alleged by petitioners and I see no reason to differ with the findings of the Tribunal in this regard.
9. Now, the only point that arise for consideration is:-

Whether the compensation granted by the Tribunal is in accordance with law or not?
10.
The accident happened in the year 2016.
The petitioners though have contended that the deceased was a Carpenter and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month have not adduced cogent reasons to prove his income.
The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the deceased at Rs.9500/- per month and which is in accordance with the chart prepared by the Lok Adalath.
Further, it is submitted that the deceased was aged 25 years at the time of accident.
Given the age of the deceased, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr [2009(6) SCC 121], multiplier of '18' is applicable.

sentences.text: Taking the income of the deceased at Rs.9,500 /- per month, 40% has to be added to his income towards future prospects as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

sentences.text: Further, the deceased who had two dependants at the time of his death, 1/3rd of his income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Thus, on the count of 'loss of dependency', the petitioners would be entitled to a sum of Rs.19,15,200/- (9500x12x18+40% x2/3).

The petitioners being the wife and son of the deceased are together entitled to a sum of Rs.80,000/-
towards 'loss of consortium'.
Further, they are entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'funeral expenses' and 'loss of estate'.
11. Thus, the compensation to the petitioners under different heads are modified as hereunder:-
AMOUNT
AMOUNT

IN RS.

1 Love and affection 20,000-00 -  Transportation, Funeral 2 expenses & loss of 35,000-00 30,000-00  estate 3 Loss of consortium 40,000-00 80,000-00 4 Loss of dependency 19,15,272-00 19,15,200-00  Total 20,10,272-00 20,25,200-00 12.

Thus, the petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.14,928/-(Rs.20,25,200/-
-Rs.20,10,272/-).

Hence, the following:
ORDER i. MFA.No.6847/2021 is allowed in part.
MFA.No.6765/2019 is dismissed.
